questions.stem: The Bhakra-Nangal Dam, India's first major multipurpose project after Independence, is built on the:
questions.explanation: Bhakra-Nangal — Sutlej. Bhakra Dam: 226 m high (one of the tallest gravity dams in the world); Govind Sagar reservoir behind it (named after Sikh guru Gobind Singh). Nangal Dam — downstream of Bhakra, smaller, regulates flow. Inaugurated 1963 by Pt Nehru — called it a 'temple of modern India'. Benefits Punjab + Haryana + Rajasthan + HP (irrigation + hydropower). Capacity: 1,325 MW. Managed by BBMB (Bhakra-Beas Management Board). Beas — Pong Dam (HP). Yamuna — Tehri (no, Tehri is on Bhagirathi); on Yamuna there's Hathnikund Barrage. Ravi — Thein/Ranjit Sagar Dam.

questions.stem: The Tehri Dam — India's TALLEST dam at 260.5 m — is built on which river?

options.option_text: Bhagirathi (a head-stream of the Ganga, in Uttarakhand)

questions.explanation: Tehri Dam — Bhagirathi River, Uttarakhand. Height 260.5 m (TALLEST dam in India; among the top 10 highest in the world). Earth + rock-fill type. Capacity 2,400 MW (one of India's largest hydropower complexes, includes Tehri pumped storage). Submerged the old Tehri town + 100+ villages — major displacement controversy in the 1980s-90s. The Bhagirathi merges with the Alaknanda at Devprayag to form the Ganga. Five Prayags (sacred confluences) along the Ganga's headwaters: Devprayag, Rudraprayag, Karnaprayag, Nandaprayag, Vishnuprayag. Mandakini joins at Rudraprayag.

questions.stem: The Nagarjuna Sagar Dam, the world's tallest masonry dam at the time of construction, is built across the:

options.option_text: Krishna (in Andhra Pradesh-Telangana border, Nalgonda + Guntur districts)

questions.explanation: Nagarjuna Sagar Dam — Krishna river, on the AP-Telangana border (post-2014 bifurcation). Height 124 m, length 1,550 m. Inaugurated 1967 (Indira Gandhi). Largest masonry dam in the world at the time. Reservoir Nagarjuna Sagar (~11 km³ live capacity). Named after Nagarjuna, the 2nd-century Buddhist scholar; the nearby site Nagarjunakonda is an important Buddhist archaeological site (now an island in the reservoir; relics relocated). Generates 815 MW + irrigates ~10 lakh hectares. Krishna's other major projects: Srisailam (upstream of Nagarjuna Sagar), Almatti, Tungabhadra (on tributary). Cauvery — Mettur Dam, Krishna Raja Sagara (KRS).

questions.stem: The Sardar Sarovar Dam, on the Narmada river, is located in which state and benefits FOUR states?

options.option_text: Madhya Pradesh; benefits MP, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan
Gujarat; benefits Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan
Maharashtra; benefits Maharashtra, MP, Goa, Karnataka
Rajasthan; benefits Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, Haryana

questions.explanation: Sardar Sarovar Dam — at Kevadia in Gujarat (Narmada district). 4-state beneficiary project: Gujarat (largest share), Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan. Cleared by Narmada Water Disputes Tribunal (1979). Foundation stone Pt Nehru 1961; full height (138.7 m) attained 2017; inaugurated by PM Modi on his 67th birthday (17 Sep 2017). Statue of Unity (Sardar Patel, 182 m, world's tallest statue) — adjacent to the dam, dedicated 31 Oct 2018. Movement against displacement: Narmada Bachao Andolan (Medha Patkar, Baba Amte, Arundhati Roy). Power 1,450 MW. Other Narmada dams: Indira Sagar (MP), Omkareshwar (MP).

questions.stem: The Mettur Dam, one of the oldest dams in India (built 1934), is on the:
questions.explanation: Mettur Dam (also known as Stanley Reservoir) — Kaveri/Cauvery river, Salem district, Tamil Nadu. Built 1934, ~215 m crest length. Inaugurated by Sir George Frederick Stanley (then Acting Governor of Madras Presidency). Major irrigation source for the Kaveri delta. Other Cauvery dams — Krishna Raja Sagara (KRS, Karnataka, Mandya district, 1932); Kabini (in Karnataka); Banasura Sagar (Kerala). Cauvery water dispute — KARNATAKA vs TAMIL NADU (with Kerala + Puducherry as parties); long-running, settled in stages by tribunal + SC; Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) constituted 2018.

questions.stem: The Idukki Dam, in Kerala — Asia's first arch dam — is built across the:
questions.explanation: Idukki Dam — Periyar river, Kerala (Idukki district). Built 1976. ASIA'S FIRST + INDIA'S FIRST arch (double-curvature) dam. Height 168 m. Construction support from Canada (CIDA). Generates 780 MW (largest hydro project in Kerala). Built between two granite hills — Kuravan + Kurathi. Periyar — 244 km, longest river of Kerala (also called the 'lifeline' of Kerala). Periyar National Park / Tiger Reserve also in this basin. Pamba — sacred river (Sabarimala). Bharathapuzha — 'Nila', second longest. Chaliyar — Kozhikode area. Other Kerala dams: Mullaperiyar (controversial, with Tamil Nadu, on the Periyar headwaters in Kerala but operated by TN since 1886 lease).

questions.stem: Match the following dams with their states/rivers — pick the WRONG pairing:
questions.explanation: Koyna is on the KOYNA river (a tributary of the Krishna), in Maharashtra — NOT directly on the Krishna. Largest hydro project of Maharashtra (2,000 MW). Located in Satara district. The 1967 Koyna earthquake (M 6.6) was a famous 'reservoir-induced seismicity' case. Other matches verify: HIRAKUD (Mahanadi, Odisha — world's longest earthen dam, 1957). TUNGABHADRA (Tungabhadra, Karnataka — built 1953, joint AP-Karnataka). RIHAND (Rihand river, a Sone tributary; UP-Sonbhadra district; reservoir is Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar).
